title: RPG dialogue interactions with NPC customers browsing shelves
description:
## Overview
NPC customers should feel alive — they should stop at shelves, look at movies, and be interactable with RPG dialogue (using the existing npc-dialogues.ts system from the other session).

## Current State
- NPCs walk waypoints in aisles but never stop at a shelf to browse
- RPG dialogue system exists for Vinny and Charlie (src/lib/npc-dialogues.ts)
- E/F key + click interaction system works
- NPCs have no interactType userData so they can't be clicked

## What Needs to Happen
1. NPCs should pause at shelves and face them (browse animation — turn toward nearest shelf, linger 5-10s)
2. NPCs get interactType='customer' userData so they're clickable
3. New dialogue trees for customers: ask what they're looking for, get recommendations, hear opinions about the genre they're browsing
4. Customer dialogue should reference the ACTUAL genre they're standing near (if near Horror shelf, they talk about horror movies)
5. Different customer personalities — the mom looking for family movies, the horror buff, the couple who can't agree, the kid who wants everything

## Reference
- Existing dialogue system: src/lib/npc-dialogues.ts (branching trees, Final Fantasy style text box)
- NPC waypoints: NPC_WAYPOINTS in Store.tsx (aisles between shelves)
- Shelf positions: SHELF_ROWS in Store.tsx (x/z positions with genre)
design:
## Technical Approach
- Add 'browse' state to NPC useFrame loop: when waitTimer triggers at a waypoint near a shelf row, rotate to face the nearest shelf and extend wait to 5-10s
- Add userData={{ interactType: 'customer', interactData: JSON.stringify({ personality: 'horror_buff' }) }} to NPC groups
- Create 4-5 customer dialogue trees in npc-dialogues.ts with genre-aware responses
- Pass the nearby genre to the dialogue system so responses are contextual
- NPC browse state: detect which shelf row (z=-3, 0, or 3) is nearest to current position, face that direction

## Browse Behavior
- At each waypoint, 40% chance to 'browse' instead of just pausing
- When browsing: rotate to face nearest shelf, extend pause to 5-10s
- While browsing: slight head movement (already exists in Charlie)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] NPCs stop at shelves and turn to face them (browse behavior)
- [ ] NPCs are clickable with E/F key showing 'Talk to Customer' label
- [ ] At least 3 different customer dialogue trees
- [ ] Dialogue references the genre the customer is near
- [ ] Different customer personalities visible in dialogue
- [ ] Browse pauses are 5-10 seconds (not the current 0.5-1s)
- [ ] Verified with security cameras — NPCs visibly facing shelves

1. **Vinny voice lines** — Greetings, movie trivia, checkout commentary
2. **NPC conversations** — Overhearing two customers discussing movies  
3. **Ambient store sounds** — Background music, VHS rewinder whir, door chime
4. **Game feedback** — Pickup sound, challenge start/complete, prop unlock fanfare

## Technical Approach  
- ElevenLabs API for text-to-speech character voices
- Pre-generate common Vinny lines, stream dynamic ones
- Spatial audio using Three.js PositionalAudio for NPC conversations
- Web Audio API for ambient loops

## Considerations
- ElevenLabs API cost — pre-generate most lines, only stream for dynamic dialogue
- Mobile: respect mute/volume settings
- Lazy load audio assets

- 7:30 PM: Store open, full brightness, all NPCs browsing

- 10:30 PM: Vinny: 'Half hour to close!' Fewer customers.
- 10:45 PM: 'Last call for rentals!'
- 11:00 PM: 'That's it, folks! We're closed!' Lights off sequence. Score screen.

## The clock on the wall should actually show the correct in-game time.
## Time displayed in HUD as well.

## If player hasn't checked out by 11 PM, Vinny kicks them out with whatever they're holding.

title: Auto visual QA pipeline — screenshot + AI eval before every layout commit
description:
## Problem
Claude makes 3D layout changes blind — writes code, commits, user catches issues. Need to close the loop.

## Solution
Build an automated QA step:
1. After any Store.tsx change, auto-capture 4 key security cameras (overhead, entrance, back_wall, counter)
2. Send screenshots to GPT-4o vision API with a focused prompt (check overlaps, floating objects, scale, orientation)
3. Parse response for FAIL/PASS items
4. If any FAILs, auto-fix before committing
5. Only commit when visual QA passes

## Implementation
- Script: `scripts/visual-qa.ts` — captures cameras, calls GPT-4o, returns pass/fail
- Hook into the Claude workflow: run visual-qa after every Store.tsx edit, before git commit
- Store reference screenshots (what 'good' looks like) for comparison
- Budget: ~$0.02 per eval (4 images at low detail)

## Also
- Keep a folder of real Blockbuster interior photos as reference
- Compare security cam shots against reference photos in the eval prompt
- Track visual regression (did this change make things WORSE?)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Script captures 4 cameras and sends to GPT-4o
- [ ] Returns structured pass/fail with specific issues
- [ ] Runs in under 30 seconds
- [ ] Claude uses this before every layout commit

title: Movie Night checkout flow — pick movies + snacks, check out with Vinny
description:
## Overview
The core game loop needs a satisfying ending. Player assembles a 'movie night': picks 1-3 movies + snacks from the store, brings them to Vinny at checkout, gets a score.

## Flow
1. Player browses shelves, picks up VHS tapes (already works — adds to inventory)
2. Player grabs snacks from counter/cooler (already works)
3. Player talks to Vinny and chooses 'Ready to check out'
4. Vinny scans each item (barcode SFX per item), comments on choices
5. Receipt screen shows: movies picked, snacks, total 'rental fee', movie night score
6. Score based on: genre variety (bonus), era match (bonus), snack pairing (comedy+popcorn=bonus), total items

## Movie Night Score
- 1 movie = 'Quick Night' (50pts base)
- 2 movies = 'Double Feature' (120pts)
- 3 movies = 'Marathon' (200pts)
- Genre variety bonus: +50 if all different genres
- Snack bonus: +25 per snack
- Era bonus: +30 if movies match the selected era
- Vinny's pick bonus: +50 if you chose a movie Vinny recommended

## After Checkout
- Summary card styled like a VHS rental receipt
- 'Come back next Friday!' message
- Option to keep browsing or 'leave the store' (return to landing page with score)
design:
## Technical
- New overlay type 'checkout' in game/page.tsx
- Vinny interaction adds 'Ready to check out' option when player has 1+ movie in inventory
- Checkout sequence: iterate held movies, play cash_register SFX per item, show Vinny comment
- Score calculation in a pure function
- Receipt component with retro dot-matrix printer styling
- High score saved to localStorage
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Player can check out with Vinny when holding 1+ movie
- [ ] Vinny comments on each movie during checkout
- [ ] Barcode/register SFX plays per item
- [ ] Receipt screen shows movies, snacks, score
- [ ] Score breakdown visible (genre variety, snacks, era match)
- [ ] High score persisted

## Overview

## Conversation Types Needed
1. **Couple arguing** about what to rent ('You ALWAYS pick action!' / 'Because your rom-coms put me to sleep!')
2. **Family argument** — mom, dad, kid all want different movies
3. **Kid begging** — kid pleading with parent, parent saying no, kid escalating
4. **Two friends debating** — sequel vs original, horror vs comedy, etc.
5. **Customer asking Vinny** — 'Do you have...?' type exchanges
6. **Nostalgic couple** — 'Remember when we saw this in theaters?'

## Implementation
- Each conversation is a sequence of {voice, text, pauseAfter} objects
- Play them in order with pauses between
- Show subtitles for each line with the speaker name
- Pick a random conversation every 30-60 seconds (replacing the current single-line system)
- Generate all clips with ElevenLabs using different voices per character in the conversation

## Voices to Use
- Roger (male, laid-back) — dad/husband
- Jessica (female, playful) — girlfriend/friend
- George (male, warm) — older customer
- Bella (female, bright) — mom/wife  
- Liam (male, energetic) — young guy/friend
- Laura (female, quirky) — friend
- Jessica-kid-settings — kid in family scenes
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At least 6 multi-line conversations (3+ lines each)
- [ ] Each conversation uses 2-3 different voices
- [ ] Conversations play as sequences with pauses between lines
- [ ] Subtitles show for each line with speaker name

title: Procedural customer requests — infinite 'help me find' quests from TMDB data
description:
## Overview
The 5 hardcoded side quests run out fast. Add procedurally generated customer requests using real TMDB movie data.

## Request Types
1. 'I'm looking for that movie with [actor]' — fetch actor's filmography from TMDB, pick one
2. 'My kid wants something about [theme]' — map to genre, pick a family-friendly movie
3. 'Do you have anything like [movie]?' — use TMDB similar movies endpoint
4. 'What's the best [genre] movie you have?' — pick highest-rated in that genre from shelf data
5. 'I need something from [year]' — filter shelf movies by release year

## How It Works
- When player talks to a customer with no active side quest, 40% chance to generate a procedural request
- Request references an ACTUAL movie that exists on the shelves (cross-reference with shelf movie registry)
- Player must find and pick up the specific movie, then return to any customer
- Reward: 25-75 XP based on difficulty
- Unlimited — new request generated each time

title: Optimize 3D store performance: instancing, LOD, texture atlas
description:
## Overview
The store renders 60+ individual VHS boxes per shelf (11 shelves = 660+ boxes), each potentially loading a poster texture. This creates hundreds of draw calls and texture loads. Need instancing and LOD for mobile performance.

## Current State
- Each VHS box is individual mesh + material + poster texture load
- PosterBox and NewReleaseVHS each do individual fetch() for poster images
- Mobile reduces to 5 boxes per shelf but still loads textures
- No geometry instancing or LOD

## Deliverables
- InstancedMesh for VHS boxes (one draw call per shelf)
- Texture atlas or shared materials for poster thumbnails
- LOD: distant shelves show simplified geometry
- Measure and document FPS improvement
design:
## Technical Approach
- Replace individual VHS meshes with InstancedMesh (drei has Instances helper)
- Create texture atlas: batch poster images into a single texture per shelf
- LOD levels: close (<5 units) = full detail, medium (5-10) = no posters, far (>10) = single colored box
- Use drei's useLOD or manual distance check in useFrame
- Frustum culling should already be on (Three.js default)

## Files
- src/components/game3d/Store.tsx — refactor ShelfUnit, PosterBox, NewReleaseVHS
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] VHS boxes use InstancedMesh (verified via Three.js inspector or draw call count)
- [ ] FPS on mobile improved by at least 10%
- [ ] Distant shelves render simplified geometry
- [ ] Visual quality at close range maintained
- [ ] No regression in interaction/click detection

description:
## Overview

## Tiers
- **Bronze** (0 XP): Default. Basic store access. Brown membership card.
- **Silver** (200 XP): Unlocks Vinny's personal recommendations. Silver card. New dialogue options.
- **Gold** (500 XP): Unlocks 'Staff Picks' section interaction. Gold card. Vinny treats you like a regular.
- **Platinum** (1000 XP): Unlocks 'Back Room' (cult/foreign films area behind Employees Only door). Platinum card. Vinny calls you by name.

## Implementation
- Add `getMembershipTier()` to game-state.ts based on total XP
- HUD shows current tier badge (colored card icon) + XP progress bar to next tier
- Vinny dialogue changes based on tier ('Hey stranger' → 'Welcome back!' → 'My favorite customer!')
- Tier-up notification with fanfare SFX when crossing threshold
- Membership card on trophy shelf changes color with tier

- `src/app/game/page.tsx` — HUD tier badge, tier-up notification
- `src/lib/npc-dialogues.ts` — tier-aware Vinny dialogue

design:

title: NPC detail: faces, outfits, animations, personality
description:
## Overview
NPCs are too blocky and generic — need more visual personality. Each NPC should be distinguishable at a glance by their outfit, hair, and body language.

## Details Needed
- **Faces**: Nose shape, eyebrows, mouth/chin variation
- **Hair**: Different styles — ponytail, buzz cut, curly, hat/cap
- **Outfits**: Recognizable clothing — flannel shirt, leather jacket, sundress, polo + khakis, hoodie
- **Accessories**: Glasses, earrings, watch, backpack, purse
- **Idle animations**: Weight shift, looking around, checking watch, scratching head
- **Walk variation**: Different walk speeds, arm swing amounts

## Constraint
Must not add significant triangle count. Target <200 triangles per NPC. Use color and shape variation, not texture complexity. No new lights or transparent materials.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each NPC has a unique, recognizable silhouette
- [ ] At least 3 different hair styles across NPCs
- [ ] At least 4 different outfit styles
- [ ] Idle animation variation (not all doing same bob)
- [ ] Kid NPC clearly reads as a kid (already started)
- [ ] No measurable FPS drop
- [ ] Verified with security cameras from multiple angles
